mozambique_channel.name: Mozambique Channel
mozambique_channel.remarks: The channel funnels a warm current south between the mainland and Madagascar, and everything that eats fish knows it.

gulf_of_guinea.name: Gulf of Guinea
gulf_of_guinea.remarks: Sits where the equator meets the prime meridian, so the point at zero degrees by zero degrees is out here in the water.

gulf_of_sidra.name: Gulf of Sidra
gulf_of_sidra.remarks: A wide bite out of the Libyan coast, with a good deal of twentieth-century military history on the bottom of it.

gulf_of_suez.name: Gulf of Suez
gulf_of_suez.remarks: Shallow, busy and littered with wrecks, several of which are among the most dived pieces of steel anywhere.

gulf_of_aqaba.name: Gulf of Aqaba
gulf_of_aqaba.remarks: Narrow, deep and bordered by four countries, with reef starting a few metres from the beach in most of them.

algeria.name: Algeria
algeria.remarks: The largest country in Africa, and about four fifths Sahara. The coast is Mediterranean and comparatively little dived.

angola.name: Angola
angola.remarks: Atlantic coast cooled by the Benguela Current, which keeps the water green, cold and full of fish.

benin.name: Benin
benin.remarks: A short stretch of surf-battered coast on the Bight of Benin, with a strong longshore current running along it.

botswana.name: Botswana
botswana.remarks: Landlocked, and the Okavango Delta drains into the desert rather than the sea — one of very few rivers anywhere that never reaches an ocean.

burkina_faso.name: Burkina Faso
burkina_faso.remarks: Landlocked and largely savannah, with the water that matters arriving once a year.

burundi.name: Burundi
burundi.remarks: Landlocked, but on Lake Tanganyika — the second deepest lake on Earth, with cichlids found nowhere else and divers who come for exactly that.

cameroon.name: Cameroon
cameroon.remarks: Coast on the Bight of Biafra, and Mount Cameroon rising straight out of it.

cape_verde.name: Cape Verde
cape_verde.remarks: Ten volcanic islands six hundred kilometres out in the Atlantic, with loggerhead turtles nesting on them in numbers that matter globally.

central_african_republic.name: Central African Republic
central_african_republic.remarks: Landlocked, forested, and drained by rivers heading for two different oceans.

chad.name: Chad
chad.remarks: Landlocked, and Lake Chad has shrunk to a fraction of the size it was within living memory.

comoros.name: Comoros
comoros.remarks: Volcanic islands in the Mozambique Channel. The coelacanth — a fish assumed extinct for sixty million years — turned up here in 1938, very much alive.

democratic_republic_of_the_congo.name: Democratic Republic of the Congo
democratic_republic_of_the_congo.remarks: Enormous, with only about forty kilometres of coast. The Congo River makes up for it by carving a canyon eight hundred metres deep into the seabed offshore.

republic_of_the_congo.name: Republic of the Congo
republic_of_the_congo.remarks: A short Atlantic coastline, and rainforest behind it for most of the country's depth.

cote_divoire.name: Cote d'Ivoire
cote_divoire.remarks: Five hundred kilometres of surf coast, with lagoons behind much of it.

djibouti.name: Djibouti
djibouti.remarks: Sits at the mouth of the Red Sea, where whale sharks gather in the Gulf of Tadjoura every winter in numbers few places match.

egypt.name: Egypt
egypt.remarks: Warm, clear water and reef down the entire Red Sea coast, plus a century of shipping that failed to notice the reef. Between them they built the country's diving industry.

equatorial_guinea.name: Equatorial Guinea
equatorial_guinea.remarks: Mainland and islands, including one volcanic island well out into the Gulf of Guinea.

eritrea.name: Eritrea
eritrea.remarks: A long Red Sea coast and the Dahlak Archipelago offshore — over three hundred islands, almost none of them inhabited.

eswatini.name: Eswatini
eswatini.remarks: Landlocked and mountainous, and entirely surrounded by two neighbours.

ethiopia.name: Ethiopia
ethiopia.remarks: Landlocked since Eritrea left, and containing the Danakil Depression, which sits over a hundred metres below sea level and is one of the hottest places on Earth.

gabon.name: Gabon
gabon.remarks: Rainforest that reaches the beach, and humpbacks calving offshore between July and September.

gambia.name: Gambia
gambia.remarks: A country shaped entirely by a river, and never more than about fifty kilometres wide.

ghana.name: Ghana
ghana.remarks: Atlantic surf coast, and Lake Volta inland — one of the largest artificial lakes anywhere, with a drowned forest still standing in it.

guinea.name: Guinea
guinea.remarks: A coast of mangrove and river mouths, and the source of the Niger somewhere behind it.

guinea_bissau.name: Guinea-Bissau
guinea_bissau.remarks: The Bijagos Archipelago offshore is a biosphere reserve, with saltwater hippopotamus in it, which is not a phrase used often.

kenya.name: Kenya
kenya.remarks: A fringing reef runs most of the coast, sheltering a lagoon behind it. The tide decides what is diveable and what is snorkelling.

lesotho.name: Lesotho
lesotho.remarks: Entirely surrounded by South Africa, and the only country in the world lying wholly above 1,400 metres.

liberia.name: Liberia
liberia.remarks: Atlantic coast with heavy surf, and a fair number of ships registered there that have never visited.

libya.name: Libya
libya.remarks: The longest Mediterranean coastline in Africa, and among the least dived.

madagascar.name: Madagascar
madagascar.remarks: Separated from everything else for something like eighty million years, with the results you would expect. Humpbacks arrive off the east coast every winter to give birth.

malawi.name: Malawi
malawi.remarks: Landlocked, but Lake Malawi holds more fish species than any other lake on Earth — most of them cichlids, most found nowhere else, and the freshwater diving is genuinely worth the trip.

mali.name: Mali
mali.remarks: Landlocked and largely desert, with the Niger looping improbably north into the Sahara before turning back.

mauritania.name: Mauritania
mauritania.remarks: Where the Sahara meets the Atlantic. The Banc d'Arguin offshore is one of the great shallow feeding grounds for migratory birds.

mauritius.name: Mauritius
mauritius.remarks: Ringed almost entirely by reef, with a lagoon inside it. Also the only place the dodo ever lived, briefly.

morocco.name: Morocco
morocco.remarks: Two coasts with completely different water: cold Atlantic upwelling on one side, Mediterranean on the other, and fourteen kilometres between them at the narrowest.

mozambique.name: Mozambique
mozambique.remarks: Two and a half thousand kilometres of coast, manta cleaning stations off Tofo, and whale sharks that turn up year round rather than seasonally.

namibia.name: Namibia
namibia.remarks: The Benguela Current keeps the water cold enough for fog to sit permanently over the Skeleton Coast, and cold enough that most of the wrecks along it are on the beach rather than under it.

niger.name: Niger
niger.remarks: Landlocked and mostly Sahara. The river it is named after clips the south-western corner.

nigeria.name: Nigeria
nigeria.remarks: The Niger Delta spreads across the coast in a fan of creeks and mangroves, and the water offshore carries the silt to prove it.

rwanda.name: Rwanda
rwanda.remarks: Landlocked and mountainous, with Lake Kivu on its western edge — a lake holding enough dissolved gas to be genuinely dangerous.

sao_tome_and_principe.name: Sao Tome and Principe
sao_tome_and_principe.remarks: Two volcanic islands almost on the equator, with clear water and very few divers in it.

senegal.name: Senegal
senegal.remarks: The westernmost point of mainland Africa, with seasonal upwelling that turns the water cold and productive.

seychelles.name: Seychelles
seychelles.remarks: Granite islands, which is odd this far out — they are the tops of a submerged continental fragment rather than volcanoes. The boulders continue underwater and make the diving.

sierra_leone.name: Sierra Leone
sierra_leone.remarks: A coast of estuaries and mangrove, with one of the largest natural harbours in the world at Freetown.

somalia.name: Somalia
somalia.remarks: The longest coastline in mainland Africa, and reef along much of it that almost nobody has dived.

south_africa.name: South Africa
south_africa.remarks: Two oceans meet at the southern tip and behave completely differently. Cold kelp forest and great whites on one side, warm reef and the sardine run on the other.

south_sudan.name: South Sudan
south_sudan.remarks: Landlocked, and containing the Sudd — a wetland so vast it swallows much of the White Nile before it can get anywhere.

sudan.name: Sudan
sudan.remarks: Red Sea reef with a fraction of Egypt's traffic. Cousteau sank an underwater habitat off Sha'ab Rumi in 1963, and parts of it are still down there.

tanzania.name: Tanzania
tanzania.remarks: Reef and drop-offs off the islands, and Lake Tanganyika inland — the second deepest lake anywhere and full of species found nowhere else.

togo.name: Togo
togo.remarks: Fifty-six kilometres of coast, which is among the shortest in Africa.

tunisia.name: Tunisia
tunisia.remarks: The Mediterranean narrows here to about a hundred and fifty kilometres between Tunisia and Sicily, which is why so much has been fought over it.

uganda.name: Uganda
uganda.remarks: Landlocked, and sharing Lake Victoria — the largest tropical lake in the world — with two neighbours.

western_sahara.name: Western Sahara
western_sahara.remarks: A long desert coast with cold, productive Atlantic water alongside it.

zambia.name: Zambia
zambia.remarks: Landlocked, and sharing Victoria Falls and Lake Kariba — the largest artificial lake by volume anywhere.

zimbabwe.name: Zimbabwe
zimbabwe.remarks: Landlocked, with Lake Kariba on its northern border and a drowned forest still standing in parts of it.

zanzibar.name: Zanzibar
zanzibar.remarks: Reef, dhows and warm water. Also the shortest war in recorded history, which lasted under forty minutes.

dahlak_archipelago.name: Dahlak Archipelago
dahlak_archipelago.remarks: Over two hundred islands in the southern Red Sea, of which fewer than five are inhabited.

aldabra.name: Aldabra
aldabra.remarks: One of the largest coral atolls on Earth, and home to more giant tortoises than the Galapagos.

reunion.name: Reunion
reunion.remarks: A volcanic island with one of the most active volcanoes anywhere, and a lagoon on its western side.

mayotte.name: Mayotte
mayotte.remarks: A double barrier reef encloses one of the largest lagoons in the Indian Ocean, with a passage through it that whales use.

saint_helena.name: Saint Helena
saint_helena.remarks: One of the remotest inhabited islands on the planet, and whale sharks turn up every summer for reasons nobody has entirely settled.
